images.title: The snack stall's samosas
images.purpose: Show a pictograph with the scale 1 icon = 10 samosas whose rows can be compared: Thursday has the most icons, and the rows give 30, 70 and 20.
images.composition: A title and an icon box at the top, and three rows of the same samosa icon for Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday, with the number of samosas written at the end of each row.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. Title Samosas sold at the snack stall left-aligned at x 80, centred on y 90, in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (44 px). ICON BOX: a white rounded rectangle (corner radius 16, dark #2B2B2B outline 4 px) x 980 to 1410, y 50 to 130, holding the text 1 icon = 10 samosas centred at (1195, 90), dark #1F2937 bold (36 px). THREE ROWS centred on y 280, 460 and 640, split by two thin construction grey #6B7280 lines (3 px) from x 60 to x 1396 at y 370 and y 550. The day names Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday are left-aligned at x 80 (dark #1F2937 bold, 40 px). Every icon is the same samosa: a rounded triangle 84 px wide and 76 px high, teal #0072B2 with a thin dark outline (3 px) and one white curved fold line; the icons of a row are in one line with their centres 100 px apart, the first centre at x 420. Row 1, Tuesday: exactly 3 icons (centres x 420, 520 and 620). Row 2, Thursday: exactly 7 icons (centres x 420, 520, 620, 720, 820, 920 and 1020). Row 3, Saturday: exactly 2 icons (centres x 420 and 520). At the end of each row, 30 px after its last icon, the number of samosas in dark #1F2937 bold (56 px), centred on the row: 30 after Tuesday (left edge x 692), 70 after Thursday (left edge x 1092) and 20 after Saturday (left edge x 592). In all there are 12 icons (3 + 7 + 2) in 3 rows. Nothing else in the frame.
labels: Samosas sold at the snack stall
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a different number of icons from 3, 7 and 2, or icons of different sizes in one pictograph
a number at the end of a row that is not 30, 70 and 20, or a total written anywhere
an icon that is cut off or drawn only in part anywhere
images.takeaway: Each row is icons times the scale: 3 icons are 30, 7 icons are 70 and 2 icons are 20, and the longest row is the most.
images.description: A pictograph of samosas sold with 1 icon = 10 samosas: Tuesday 3 icons (30), Thursday 7 icons (70) and Saturday 2 icons (20).
images.context: Concept image for Comparing with a Pictograph. It follows the idea of the pictograph in your maths book (rows of one icon with an icon box) and uses the numbers of this concept's own example: 3, 7 and 2 icons with a scale of 10.
images.teaching_notes: Let the student find the longest row first, then read each row as icons times 10 and find the differences. The slip to watch: saying Thursday has 7 samosas instead of 70.

image_decisions.why: A pictograph with the scale 10 and three rows of different length gives the student something to compare, and the numbers at the row ends check the reading.
